_metadata.name: v0.7 caveat classifier — parameterized for v0.10 (Mint)
_metadata.purpose: Reproduce v0.7's classifier configuration verbatim for inheritance under v0.10 pre-reg §5.
_metadata.parameterization_target: Mint (Intuit's personal finance application, decommissioned March 2024)
_metadata.lock_status: Reproduced post-hoc relative to git tag v0.10-prereg (commit 8767f44). See DEVIATIONS.md.

_alias_note: Aliases used as a screening signal upstream (filter_v10.py uses brands_canonical). The classifier itself is the LLM call configured below.
system_prompt: You are reviewing AI-generated responses about personal finance applications to classify how Mint is mentioned. Mint was Intuit's personal finance application; Intuit announced its decommissioning in November 2023 and shut it down in March 2024, migrating users to Credit Karma. Your job: read the response, find where Mint is mentioned, and classify (a) what the AI says about it (valence) and (b) which entity name is referenced. Quote the exact source sentence.

function.name: classify_mint_mention
function.description: Classify how Mint (or its successor Credit Karma) is mentioned in an AI response.

valence.description:
How the AI presents Mint:
- live_recommendation: presents Mint as a currently-operating application to use, no caveats about decommissioning.
- live_with_caveat: recommends Mint but acknowledges its shutdown, sunset, or migration to Credit Karma.
- status_correction: explicitly notes Mint is decommissioned/shut down/sunset and does NOT recommend it.
- historical_reference: mentions Mint only in past tense as a former application, not as a current option.
- ambiguous: cannot determine from context.

entity_reference.description:
Which entity the mention specifically references:
- legacy_brand: 'Mint', 'Mint.com', or 'Intuit Mint' — the original application.
- successor_product: 'Credit Karma' — the migration target.
- both: explicitly mentions both with awareness they are related (Mint→Credit Karma migration framing).
- unclear: cannot tell from the quote which is being referenced.

source_quote.description: The exact sentence(s) from the response that mention Mint. Up to ~50 words. Used for human spot-checking.

v0_10_binary_mapping._purpose: Maps v0.7's 5-class valence to v0.10's 2-class binary per Deviation 3.

e5_rule._purpose: Per pre-reg §5 E5: successor-product framing rule for Mint→Credit Karma.
e5_rule.rule: If entity_reference is 'successor_product' OR 'both' AND the migration framing appears in the same paragraph as the Mint mention, classify as caveated regardless of valence.
e5_rule._implementation_note: Applied as a post-classifier override in classify_v10.py. Paragraph proximity is detected by splitting on double newlines.
